A SMALL NOTE ABOUT THE WORLD

An atlas with honest edges.

Country and territory outlines and first-level boundaries come from Natural Earth (public domain). Cities and towns come from GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), with a documented population threshold and some administrative seats. China municipality district outlines additionally use geoBoundaries / © OpenStreetMap contributors (2017 snapshot, ODbL). The compiled geographic database is available under ODbL 1.0. These are map records, not a complete register of every settlement.

Native names appear when supplied or matched to a regional language. An English or source-name fallback is identified when a native label is unavailable. Some places have several official languages.

Boundaries are generalized, may be dated, and follow the source’s cartographic convention. Country lists include territories and disputed map units; their appearance is not a statement of sovereignty. Your atlas groups Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan within China, giving 34 province-level units. This is a customized navigation convention.

Progress is the number of visited immediate children divided by the number of included children in the current view. A parent and its children are marked independently. Visiting a province does not automatically mark its cities.

Your progress stays in this browser profile on this device. It is restored when you return, and is not shared between profiles. Clearing site storage removes it. Export a copy to keep a backup.
